subject: Scaling multiple covariates after adding them to habitat mask

messages.author: 1661308b34ed6271
messages.subject: Scaling multiple covariates after adding them to habitat mask
parts:
Hi Murray,

I am trying to scale my spatial covariates by using the scale function. I have added three covariates to my habitat mask list: elevation, ndvi, and ruggedness. I am unable to access and scale the covariates using the lapply function. Could you check what step I am getting wrong?

Many thanks,
Manvi

Here is the code:

#Adding all the three covariates to same mask list
masks1 <-make.mask(traps(msSL1), buffer = 25000, type = 'trapbuffer')
covmask.list<-masks1
for(i in 1:10){
  covmask.list[[i]]<-addCovariates(masks1[[i]], hp_ele_grid)
}
for(i in 1:10){
  covmask.list[[i]]<-addCovariates(covmask.list[[i]], hp_ndvi_grid)
}
for(i in 1:10){
  covmask.list[[i]]<-addCovariates(covmask.list[[i]], hp_rug_grid)
}
#after adding covariates, scaling them
covariates(covmask.list)<-lapply(covariates(covmask.list), scale)

#this does not throw an error, but the covariates don't get scaled. If I run only lapply(covariates(covmask.list), scale, I get scaled values of all variables:

messages.subject: Re: Scaling multiple covariates after adding them to habitat mask
parts:
Look closely at this example:

library(secr)
masks <- make.mask(traps(ovenCH), buffer = 250, type = 'trapbuffer')
for (i in 1:5) covariates(masks[[i]]) <- data.frame(random = runif(nrow(masks[[i]])))
lapply(covariates(masks), summary)

$`2005`
     random         
 Min.   :0.0002118  
 1st Qu.:0.2386970  
 Median :0.4903815  
 Mean   :0.4931053  
 3rd Qu.:0.7447533  
 Max.   :0.9999955 
etc.

for (i in 1:5) covariates(masks[[i]]) <- scale(covariates(masks[[i]]))
lapply(covariates(masks), summary)

etc.
